Main.sentence: Bruce Frederick Joseph Springsteen (born September 23, 1949) is an American musician.

Nicknamed " ___E:the Boss U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorific_nicknames_in_popular_music#S)___ ", Springsteen has released 21 studio albums spanning six decades; most of his albums feature the ___E:E Street Band U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_Street_Band)___ , his backing band since 1972. Springsteen is a pioneer of ___E:heartland rock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_rock)___ , combining commercially successful rock with poetic, socially conscious lyrics that reflect ___E:working class American life U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_class_in_the_United_States)___ .
He is known for his energetic concerts, some of which last more than four hours.

Springsteen released his first two albums, Greetings from Asbury Park, N.J. and The Wild, the Innocent & the E Street Shuffle , in 1973. Although both were well received by critics, neither earned him a large audience.
He changed his style and achieved worldwide popularity with Born to Run (1975).
Springsteen followed with Darkness on the Edge of Town (1978) and The River (1980), Springsteen's first album to top the ___E:Billboard 200 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200)___ chart.

After the solo acoustic album Nebraska (1982), he recorded Born in the U.S.A. (1984) with the E Street Band, which became his most commercially successful album and the ___E:23rd-best selling album ever U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_albums)___ as of 2024. All seven singles from Born in the U.S.A. reached the Top 10 of the ___E:Billboard Hot 100 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100)___ , including the ___E:title track U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_in_the_U.S.A._(song))___ .
Springsteen mostly hired session musicians for the recording of his next three albums, Tunnel of Love (1987), Human Touch (1992), and Lucky Town (1992).
He reassembled the E Street Band for Greatest Hits (1995), and recorded the acoustic album The Ghost of Tom Joad (1995) and the EP Blood Brothers (1996) solo.
Springsteen then released The Rising (2002), which was dedicated to the victims of the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ .
He released two more folk albums, Devils & Dust (2005) and We Shall Overcome: The Seeger Sessions (2006), his first cover album.
Springsteen followed with two more albums with the E Street Band, Magic (2007) and Working on a Dream (2009).
His next albums, Wrecking Ball (2012) and High Hopes (2014), topped album charts worldwide.

In 2017, 2018 and 2021, Springsteen performed the critically acclaimed show Springsteen on Broadway , in which he performed songs and told stories from ___E:his 2016 autobiography U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_to_Run_(autobiography))___ ; an ___E:album version U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springsteen_on_Broadway_(album))___ from the ___E:Broadway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre)___ performances was released in 2018. He released the solo album Western Stars in 2019, Letter to You with the E Street Band in 2020, and a solo covers album entitled Only the Strong Survive in 2022. Letter to You reached No. 2 in the US, making Springsteen the first artist to release a top-five album in six consecutive decades.

A prominent musician from the ___E:album era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album_era)___ , Springsteen has sold more 140 million records worldwide, making him one of the ___E:best-selling music artists of all time U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best-selling_music_artists_of_all_time)___ . ___E:His accolades U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bruce_Springsteen)___ include 20 ___E:Grammy Awards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award)___ , two ___E:Golden Globes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe)___ , an ___E:Academy Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award)___ , and a ___E:Special Tony Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Tony_Award)___ .

He was inducted into the ___E:Songwriters Hall of Fame U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame)___ and the ___E:Rock and Roll Hall of Fame U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame)___ in 1999, received the ___E:Kennedy Center Honors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors)___ in 2009, was named ___E:MusiCares U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusiCares)___ person of the year in 2013, and was awarded the ___E:Presidential Medal of Freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom)___ in 2016 and the ___E:National Medal of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts)___ in 2023. In 2010, Rolling Stone ranked Springsteen 23rd on its list of the " ___E:100 Greatest Artists of All Time U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone%27s_100_Greatest_Artists_of_All_Time)___ ", describing him as "the embodiment of rock and roll".

In 2025, Springsteen became one of only five artists to gross over $2.3 billion in touring thanks to his ___E:2023-2025 Tour U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springsteen_and_E_Street_Band_2023_Tour)___ with the E Street Band.

Springsteen was born at ___E:Monmouth Medical Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monmouth_Medical_Center)___ in ___E:Long Branch, New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Branch,_New_Jersey)___ , on September 23, 1949,  to Douglas Frederick "Dutch" Springsteen (1924–1998) and his wife, Adele Ann (née Zerilli; 1925–2024).

Springsteen's father   worked as a bus driver and other jobs.  His father had mental health issues throughout his life, which worsened in his later life.  His mother, who was originally from the ___E:Bay Ridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_Ridge)___ neighborhood of ___E:Brooklyn, New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York)___ ,  worked as a legal secretary and was the family's main breadwinner.

He is of Dutch, Irish, and Italian descent,  and grew up ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic)___ in ___E:Freehold, New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freehold_Borough,_New_Jersey)___ .

Springsteen's paternal ancestors were among the early Dutch families who, in the 17th century, settled in ___E:colonial-era America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_history_of_the_United_States)___ , then part of the ___E:Dutch Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Republic)___ known as ___E:New Netherland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland)___ .

Springsteen's paternal ancestor, John Springsteen, was a ___E:patriot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot_(American_Revolution))___ in the ___E:American Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution)___ , which evolved into the ___E:Continental Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Army)___ during the ___E:American Revolutionary War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War)___ .

The Springsteen surname originates in ___E:Groningen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groningen_(province))___ , a province in the ___E:Netherlands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands)___ ,  and is ___E:topographic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topographic_name)___ , translating to "jump stone" and meaning a ___E:stepping stone U:(https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/stepping_stone)___ used on unpaved streets or between two houses.

Springsteen's Italian maternal grandfather was born in ___E:Vico Equense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vico_Equense)___ and emigrated through ___E:Ellis Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island)___ .
He arrived in the United States unable to read or write English, but went on to become a lawyer and impressed the young Springsteen as being "larger than life".
Springsteen has two younger sisters, Virginia and ___E:Pamela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Springsteen)___ (born c. 1962).
Pamela Springsteen worked briefly as an actress and later as a photographer; she took photos for three Springsteen albums, Human Touch , Lucky Town , and The Ghost of Tom Joad .

Springsteen attended the St. Rose of Lima Catholic School in Freehold, where he was at odds with the nuns and rebelled against the strictures imposed upon him, though some of his later music reflected a Catholic ethos and included ___E:Irish Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholic)___ hymns with a rock music twist.
In 2012, Springsteen said that it was his Catholic upbringing rather than his political ideology that most influenced his music.
He said his faith gave him a "very active spiritual life" but joked that this "made it very difficult sexually" and added "once a Catholic, always a Catholic".

He grew up hearing fellow New Jersey singer ___E:Frank Sinatra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra)___ on the radio, and became interested in being a musician by the age of seven after seeing ___E:Elvis Presley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley)___ 's performances on The Ed Sullivan Show in 1956 and 1957. Soon after, his mother rented him a guitar from Mike Diehl's Music in Freehold for $6 a week and took a few weeks of guitar lessons, but quit after it failed to provide him with the instant gratification he desired.
In ninth grade, Springsteen entered ___E:Freehold High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freehold_High_School)___ , a public high school, but did not fit in there either.
A former teacher said Springsteen was a "loner who wanted nothing more than to play his guitar".
He graduated in 1967, but felt so alienated that he skipped his graduation ceremony.

He briefly attended ___E:Ocean County College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_County_College)___ , but dropped out.  At age 19, Springsteen was ___E:called for his draft physical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States)___ , but failed it because of a ___E:concussion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion)___ he suffered in a motorcycle accident two years earlier combined with his behavior at induction, both of which reportedly made him unacceptable for ___E:military service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_service)___ .
In failing his examination, Springsteen likely avoided service in the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ .

In 1969, when he was 20 years old, Springsteen's parents and sister Pamela moved to ___E:San Mateo, California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo,_California)___ ; he and his sister Virginia, who was married and pregnant at the time, remained in Freehold.
In 1964, Springsteen saw ___E:the Beatles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles)___ ' televised appearances on The Ed Sullivan Show .
Inspired, he bought his first guitar for $18.95 at the ___E:Western Auto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Auto)___ appliance store.
Thereafter, he started playing for audiences with a band called the Rogues at local venues, including ___E:Elks Lodge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elks_Lodge)___ in Freehold.
Later that year, his mother took out a loan to buy him a $60 ___E:Kent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent_(guitar))___ guitar, an act he later memorialized in his song "The Wish".

In 1965, he went to the house of Tex and Marion Vinyard, who sponsored young bands in town. They helped him become the lead guitarist and subsequently one of the lead singers of ___E:the Castiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Castiles)___ , a band that recorded two original songs at a public recording studio in ___E:Brick Township U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brick_Township)___ and played a variety of venues, including ___E:Cafe Wha? U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cafe_Wha%3F)___ in ___E:Greenwich Village U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Village)___ .

Marion Vinyard said she believed the young Springsteen when he promised he would make it big.   In the late 1960s, Springsteen performed briefly in a ___E:power trio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_trio)___ known as Earth, who played in various clubs in New Jersey and at a major show at the Hotel Diplomat in ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ .

From 1969 through early 1971, Springsteen performed with the band Child, which later changed its name to ___E:Steel Mill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel_Mill)___ and included ___E:Danny Federici U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Federici)___ , ___E:Vini Lopez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vini_Lopez)___ , ___E:Vinnie Roslin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinnie_Roslin)___ , and later ___E:Steven Van Zandt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Van_Zandt)___ and ___E:Robbin Thompson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbin_Thompson)___ .

Steel Mill performed at various ___E:Jersey Shore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_Shore)___ venues and also outside of New Jersey, in ___E:Richmond, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia)___ ;  ___E:Nashville, Tennessee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee)___ ; and ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ ,  and gathered a cult following.

In his January 1970 review of Steel Mill's show at ___E:The Matrix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix_(club))___ , music critic Philip Elwood wrote in the San Francisco Examiner that he had "never been so overwhelmed by a totally unknown talent"  and called Steel Mill "the first big thing that's happened to ___E:Asbury Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asbury_Park)___ since the good ship ___E:Morro Castle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Morro_Castle_(1930))___ burned to the waterline of that Jersey beach in '34".
Elwood praised the band's "cohesive musicality" and called Springsteen "a most impressive composer".
In ___E:San Mateo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo,_California)___ , Steel Mill recorded three original Springsteen songs at Pacific Recording.

This was different, shifted the lay of the land. Four guys, playing and singing, writing their own material. [...] Rock 'n' roll came to my house where there seemed to be no way out [...] and opened up a whole world of possibilities.

As Springsteen sought to shape a unique and genuine musical and lyrical style, he performed with the bands Dr. Zoom & the Sonic Boom from early-to-mid-1971, the Sundance Blues Band in mid-1971, and the Bruce Springsteen Band from mid-1971 to mid-1972.  His songwriting ability included, as his future record label described it in early publicity campaigns, "more words in some individual songs than other artists had in whole albums".

He brought his skills to the attention of several people who went on to prove influential to his career development, including managers ___E:Mike Appel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Appel)___ and Jim Cretecos, who in turn brought him to the attention of ___E:John Hammond U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hammond_(record_producer))___ , a talent scout at ___E:Columbia Records U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records)___ .
In May 1972, Springsteen auditioned for Hammond.
In October 1972, Springsteen formed a new band for the recording of his debut album, Greetings from Asbury Park, N.J.

The band eventually became known as the ___E:E Street Band U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_Street_Band)___ , although the name was not used until September 1974.   Springsteen acquired the nickname "the Boss" during this period, since he took on the task of collecting his band's nightly pay and distributing it among his bandmates.
The nickname also reportedly sprang from games of Monopoly , which Springsteen played with other Jersey Shore musicians.

Springsteen was signed to ___E:Columbia Records U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records)___ in 1972 by John Hammond, who had signed ___E:Bob Dylan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan)___ to the same label a decade earlier.
His debut album, Greetings from Asbury Park, N.J. , was released in January 1973, establishing him as a critical favorite.

Because of Springsteen's lyrical poeticism and ___E:folk rock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_rock)___ -rooted music exemplified on tracks like " ___E:Blinded by the Light U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinded_by_the_Light)___ " and " ___E:For You U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_You_(Bruce_Springsteen_song))___ ", and his connection with Hammond and Columbia Records, critics initially compared Springsteen to ___E:Bob Dylan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan)___ . "He sings with a freshness and urgency I haven't heard since I was rocked by ' ___E:Like a Rolling Stone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_a_Rolling_Stone)___ '", Crawdaddy magazine editor ___E:Peter Knobler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Knobler)___ wrote in a March 1973 profile of Springsteen's that included photographs taken by ___E:Ed Gallucci U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Gallucci)___ .

Crawdaddy was an early champion of Springsteen; Knobler profiled him in the magazine three times, in 1973, 1975, and 1978.  In June 1976, Springsteen and the E Street Band acknowledged the magazine's support by giving a private performance at the magazine's 10th Anniversary Party in New York City.
Springsteen's second album, The Wild, the Innocent & the E Street Shuffle , was released in November 1973, eleven months after Greetings from Asbury Park .
Like Springsteen's inaugural album, The Wild, the Innocent & the E Street Shuffle was met with critical acclaim but limited commercial success.

Springsteen's songs became grander in form and scope with the E Street Band providing a less folksy, more ___E:rhythm and blues U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues)___ vibe, and lyrics that romanticized teenage street life. " ___E:4th of July, Asbury Park (Sandy) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_of_July,_Asbury_Park_(Sandy))___ " and "Incident on 57th Street" became fan favorites, while " ___E:Rosalita (Come Out Tonight) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosalita_(Come_Out_Tonight))___ " continues to rank among Springsteen's most beloved concert numbers. "Rosalita" is the ninth-most played song in Springsteen's concert catalog; as of June 2020, he has played it live 809 times.

In February 1974, ___E:the Stone Pony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Stone_Pony)___ , a music venue and bar, opened on Ocean Avenue in ___E:Asbury Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asbury_Park)___ , and Springsteen played there regularly.

Several years later, in the early 1980s, prior to the start of the ___E:Born in the U.S.A. Tour U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_in_the_U.S.A._Tour)___ in June 1984, Springsteen also met his second and current wife ___E:Patti Scialfa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patti_Scialfa)___ at the Stone Pony during her performance there.

A regular venue for Springsteen, ___E:Jon Bon Jovi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Bon_Jovi)___ , ___E:Southside Johnny U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southside_Johnny)___ , and other acts from the area, the Stone Pony has since been described as "an integral part of music history for decades."

After seeing Springsteen's performance at the Harvard Square Theater in 1974, music critic ___E:Jon Landau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Landau)___ wrote that he "saw rock and roll future, and its name is Bruce Springsteen."  Springsteen met Landau in Boston a month prior and the two became close friends;   Landau subsequently became the co-producer of Springsteen's next album, Born to Run , in February 1975.   As Springsteen's last-ditch effort at a commercially viable record, Springsteen became bogged down in the recording process while striving for a " ___E:Wall of Sound U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_of_Sound)___ " production.

When his manager, ___E:Mike Appel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Appel)___ , orchestrated the release of an early mix of " ___E:Born to Run U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_to_Run_(song))___ " to nearly a dozen radio stations, anticipation built toward the album's release.
The album took over 14 months to record, with six months spent recording "Born to Run" alone.

E Street Band members David Sancious and Ernest Carter departed after "Born to Run" was completed, and were replaced by ___E:Roy Bittan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Bittan)___ and ___E:Max Weinberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Weinberg)___ on piano and drums, respectively.
Springsteen battled with anger and frustration throughout the sessions, saying he heard "sounds in [his] head" that he could not explain to the others in the studio.
He also dealt with two producers who had opposing views.

During the recording of " ___E:Tenth Avenue Freeze-Out U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenth_Avenue_Freeze-Out)___ ", Steven Van Zandt conceived the horn parts for the horn players on the spot in the studio after Springsteen and Bittan had failed to write proper ones by the time the players arrived to record.
He joined the E Street Band shortly thereafter.
Mixing for Born to Run lasted until July 20, 1975, just before a concert tour began.

Born to Run was mastered while the band was on the road. Springsteen was furious at the initial acetate, throwing it into the swimming pool of the hotel he was staying at. He contemplated scrapping the entire project and re-recording it live before he was stopped by Landau.
Springsteen was sent multiple mixes as he was on the road and rejected all of them until August when he approved the final one.

Born to Run was released in August 1975. It proved to be a breakthrough album    that catapulted Springsteen to worldwide fame.  The album peaked at No. 3 on the ___E:Billboard Top LPs & Tape U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200)___ chart, eventually going seven times platinum in the US.  The album's two singles, "Born to Run" and "Tenth Avenue Freeze-Out" reached No. 23 and 83, respectively, on the Billboard Hot 100.   According to author Louis Masur, the album's success was tied to the fears of growing old held by a generation of late teenagers.

In October 1975, Springsteen appeared on the covers of both Newsweek and Time in the same week, becoming the first artist to do so.  The magazines' cover stories resulted in a media backlash,  as critics began wondering if Springsteen was for real or the product of record company promotion.
Springsteen was hurt by the backlash  and disliked his newfound attention.

When the E Street Band arrived in London for their first concerts outside North America,  Springsteen personally tore down promotional posters in the lobby of the ___E:Hammersmith Odeon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammersmith_Odeon)___ .

A legal battle with Appel kept Springsteen out of the studio for nearly a year, during which time he kept the E Street Band together through ___E:extensive touring across the U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_to_Run_tours)___ and continued writing new material.
Reaching a settlement with Appel in May 1977,  Springsteen returned to the studio, and the subsequent nine-month recording sessions with the E Street Band produced Darkness on the Edge of Town .
The record stripped the "Wall of Sound" production of Born to Run   for a rawer ___E:hard rock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock)___ sound.
Its lyrics focus on ill-fortuned people who fight back against overwhelming odds.
Released in June 1978,  Darkness on the Edge of Town sold fewer copies than its predecessor,  but remained on the Billboard chart for 167 weeks, selling three million copies in the U.S.

Its three singles—" ___E:Prove It All Night U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prove_It_All_Night)___ ", " ___E:Badlands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badlands_(song))___ ", and " ___E:The Promised Land U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Promised_Land_(Bruce_Springsteen_song))___ "—performed modestly.
The supporting ___E:Darkness Tour U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkness_Tour)___ was Springsteen's largest up to that point and featured shows that lasted upwards of three hours in length.
The staff of Ultimate Classic Rock said the tour solidified Springsteen and the E Street Band as "one of the most exciting live acts in rock 'n' roll".

By the late 1970s, Springsteen earned a reputation as a songwriter whose material could provide hits for other bands. ___E:Manfred Mann's Earth Band U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manfred_Mann%27s_Earth_Band)___ had achieved a U.S.

No. 1 pop hit with a heavily rearranged version of Greetings ' "Blinded by the Light" in early 1977. ___E:Patti Smith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patti_Smith)___ reached No. 13 with her version of Springsteen's unreleased " ___E:Because the Night U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Because_the_Night)___ " with revised lyrics by Smith in 1978. ___E:The Pointer Sisters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pointer_Sisters)___ hit No. 2 in 1979 with Springsteen's then unreleased " ___E:Fire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_(Bruce_Springsteen_song))___ ".
